headline: THE ROUND'S CLAIM IS TRUE AT THE FRAME IT MEASURES. My own live sweep of all 115 doors: 0 bodies inside a drawn building one frame after exitInterior(). Offline, independently: 0 of 113 declared doorsteps satisfy insideBuilding().

AND IT STOPS BEING TRUE AT FRAME 30. Same 115 doors at 1/30/120/600 fixed steps: 0 / 8 / 10 / 10. The solver slides the body 0.5-8.9 m into a neighbour and it rests there. Ten rooms named in the verdict.

RE-ENTRY REGRESSED AND THE ROUND'S NUMBER FOR IT IS WRONG IN KIND. doorAt() returns the NEAREST door of the town; the round's rollup counts door_in_reach truthy and publishes 106. Pressing interact through the real latch: 96 back into the room you left, 10 into a DIFFERENT building, 9 into nothing — against 108/5/2 with the derivation cut. Moving 112 doors onto entry walls put four pairs of Blackrose doors 1.00 m apart. Reproduced offline and live, identical numbers.

THE PROP COUNT IS MEASURED BY A PREDICATE THE ROUND DID NOT DESCRIBE. Its words say 'reaches more than 0.6 m outside'; its code computes how far the box sits WHOLLY CLEAR, which is 0 whenever the box still overlaps the room. At 1fda355: 61 meshes in 49 rooms under overhang (all prop:hel_shell_roof), 0 under clearance. The round-4 verdict DID state its tolerance (0.6 m, §4(c)) — the builder's status file says it did not.

THE NEXT BLIND SET, inside the fix for the first: applyInteriorBounds()'s orphan pass does `if (!plan) continue` ABOVE its own counter, so barge-hold and writ-house (settlement 'tidewrack', not one of the 8 documents) are reached by NO offline loop in this piece — including the fail-closed check the round shipped. Only the live sweep sees them.

THE LAMP FIX IS REAL AND I STRENGTHENED IT. Confirmed by the round-4 critic's own instrument re-run at HEAD (C3 = 0), and demonstrated at an ENTITY: lamps in place -> enemy alert 100 AGGRO; every lamp 60 m away -> 80 SUSPICIOUS; restored -> 100.
